### From endo packages/immutable-arraybuffer/{src/immutable-arraybuffer-pony.js,src/immutable-arraybuffer-shim.js,README.md} (Cycle 201 chat-lane; 350 source (253 ponyfill + 97 shim) + 75 README; §thirty-fifth consecutive designs/chat alternation cycle 166-201; §nineteenth-member of §small-files-with-large-knowledge-density family; **single most structurally interesting move**: §Ponyfill-plus-Shim full-version (sibling to cycle 197 panic's ponyfill-only deferred-shim) + §Purposeful-Violation section explicitly named in README + §WeakMap-as-emulated-private-field-AND-brand-check (Hermes-no-class-private-fields) + §intermediate-prototype-`ImmutableArrayBufferInternalPrototype`-inheriting-from-ArrayBuffer.prototype + §three-tier-fallback-with-three-platform-degradation + §two-named-motivations-from-orthogonal-domains; §Ponyfill (index.js) defines and exports new things without modifying old (`transferBufferToImmutable`/`sliceBufferToImmutable`/`isBufferImmutable`); §Shim (shim.js) modifies existing JavaScript primordials by adding `transferToImmutable`/`sliceToImmutable`/`immutable` to ArrayBuffer.prototype; §two-named-policies-for-the-shim: §modern-shim-practice-frowns-on-conditional-installation (so changes to the proposal don't break old code depending on old shim) — warn-and-continue if detecting prior installation; §shim-still-runs-after-native-implementation (will require a later manual step to delete the shim, after manual analysis of the compat implications); §Purposeful-Violation section: `Symbol.toStringTag = 'ImmutableArrayBuffer'` (not 'ArrayBuffer') reduces fidelity but defeats concordance's `toString()` sniff (Ava's diagnostic library; concordance would otherwise assume the object is a genuine ArrayBuffer and try `Buffer.from`); §the-pattern: when-you-must-violate-fidelity-name-the-violation-and-its-rationale; §six+-named-Caveats in README: (1) platform-degradation (Hermes, Node ≤16, some JavaScriptCore — neither structuredClone nor ArrayBuffer.prototype.transfer); (2) no-intermediate-prototype-in-proposal; (3) intermediate-prototype-discoverable-not-encapsulated; (4) not-real-exotic-objects (cannot be DataView/TypedArray backing stores); (5) cannot-be-cloned-or-transferred-between-JS-threads; (6) shim-still-runs-after-native-implementation; (7) not-hardened-by-itself — the ses-shim is expected to import and treat as additional primordials to be hardened during lockdown's harden phase; §WeakMap-as-emulated-private-field with explicit honest acknowledgment "If we could use classes with private fields everywhere, this would have been a `this.#buffer` private field on an `ImmutableArrayBufferInternal` class. But we cannot do so on Hermes" — §the-WeakMap-emulates-the-private-field-AND-the-brand-check; §three-different-ways-to-emulate-private-state in JavaScript across @endo: §pumpkin-sentinel (cycle 199 memoize) + §registered-symbol (cycle 197 panic) + §WeakMap (this cycle); §the-WeakMap-approach-is-the-only-one-that-also-serves-as-brand-check by-construction; §method-binding-pre-defineProperty on the WeakMap (`buffers.has = buffers.has` etc) to avoid post-hoc prototype lookups (defense against prototype tampering); §intermediate-prototype `ImmutableArrayBufferInternalPrototype.__proto__ = arrayBufferPrototype` — §emulated-immutable-buffers-inherit-from-ArrayBuffer.prototype-transitively so `x instanceof ArrayBuffer` acts as proposed; §five-throw-methods on intermediate prototype (resize / transfer / transferToFixedLength / transferToImmutable + slice stays mutable but sliceToImmutable returns new immutable) + §six-getter-overrides (byteLength / detached false / maxByteLength / resizable false / immutable true / toStringTag); §two-distinct-throw-messages — "Cannot resize an immutable ArrayBuffer" for resize; "Cannot detach an immutable ArrayBuffer" for transfer/transferToFixedLength/transferToImmutable — §two-error-categories with named-rationale; §brand-check-via-`getBuffer(this)` on every accessor — even getters that don't need the buffer-value call it for the side-effect (the throw on non-emulated instances); §slice-stays-mutable-vs-sliceToImmutable distinguishes mutable-copy from new-immutable; §three-tier-fallback for transfer mechanism: `ArrayBuffer.prototype.transfer` (Node 21+) → `structuredClone({transfer: [...]})` (Node 17+) → undefined (graceful degradation; ponyfill+shim fail to initialize on known-deficient platforms); §zero-length-slice-as-genuine-ArrayBuffer-enforcement — `arrayBufferSlice(arrayBuffer, 0, 0)` before structuredClone (the side-effect is enforcing arrayBuffer is a genuine exotic object; comment "Hopefully, a zero-length slice is cheap, but still enforces that arrayBuffer is a genuine ArrayBuffer exotic object" — §honest-comment-naming-cost-uncertainty); §capture-before-scuttled pre-lockdown discipline — eight intrinsics captured at module load (ArrayBuffer / Object / Reflect / Symbol / TypeError / Uint8Array / WeakMap / structuredClone) with named comment "Capture structuredClone before it can be scuttled"; §belt-and-suspenders-freeze on must-not-escape factory `makeImmutableArrayBufferInternal` — comment names that it must not escape (module exports only high-level functions, not the internal factory); freeze provides defense-in-depth; §warning-not-error-when-overwriting prior installation: §"Modern shim practice frowns on conditional installation, at least for proposals prior to stage 3. This is so changes to the proposal since an old shim was distributed don't need to worry about the proposal breaking old code depending on the old shim. Thus, if we detect that we're about to overwrite a prior installation, we simply issue this warning and continue"; §TODO-comment naming the known-broken-interaction with lockdown's frozen primordials ("if the primordials are frozen after the prior implementation, such as by lockdown, then this precludes overwriting as expected. However, for this case, the following warning text will be confusing"); §encapsulated-genuine-ArrayBuffer-with-exclusive-access — security demands exclusive access; immutability enforced by never modifying it; §two-named-motivations from orthogonal domains: (1) §ROM-vs-RAM Moddable XS rationale — "Some JavaScript implementations, like Moddable XS, bring JavaScript to embedded systems, like device controllers, where ROM is much more plentiful and cheaper than RAM. These systems need to place voluminous fixed data into ROM, and currently do so using semantics outside the official JavaScript standard"; (2) §By-copy network protocol rationale — "The OCapN network protocol treats strings and byte-arrays as distinct forms of bulk data to be transmitted by copy. At JavaScript endpoints speaking OCapN such as `@endo/pass-style` + `@endo/marshal`, JavaScript strings represent OCapN strings. The immutability of strings in the JavaScript language reflects their by-copy nature in the protocol. Likewise, to reflect an OCapN byte-array well into the JavaScript language, we need an immutable container of bulk binary data"; §two-motivations-from-orthogonal-domains converging on the same primitive as §the-shape-of-a-proposal-rationale; §plain-JavaScript-not-Hardened-JavaScript disclaimer — "Thus, the objects and function it creates are not hardened by this ponyfill/shim itself. Rather, the ses-shim is expected to import these, and then treat the resulting objects as if they were additional primordials, to be hardened during lockdown's harden phase"; §the-Eval-Twin-Problem-chain extends implicitly to this package; §tier-1 borrowing: §Ponyfill+Shim-pattern-full-version + §Purposeful-Violation-section-in-README + §concordance-sniff-defense-via-Symbol.toStringTag + §six+-named-Caveats-as-honest-enumeration-of-limitations + §WeakMap-as-emulated-private-field-AND-brand-check + §method-binding-pre-defineProperty + §intermediate-prototype-inheriting-from-the-host-prototype + §five-throw-methods-on-immutable-prototype-with-two-distinct-error-messages + §slice-stays-mutable-vs-sliceToImmutable-distinction + §brand-check-via-`getBuffer(this)`-on-every-accessor + §three-tier-fallback-with-named-known-deficient-platforms + §zero-length-slice-as-genuine-ArrayBuffer-enforcement + §capture-before-scuttled + §belt-and-suspenders-freeze-on-must-not-escape-factory + §modern-shim-practice-frowns-on-conditional-installation + §shim-still-runs-after-native-implementation + §warning-not-error-when-overwriting-with-TODO-naming-broken-lockdown-interaction + §two-named-motivations-from-orthogonal-domains + §plain-JavaScript-not-Hardened-JavaScript-disclaimer + §encapsulated-genuine-ArrayBuffer-with-exclusive-access; §synthesis-target: slot machine library §immutable-game-state-shapes can §borrow-the-WeakMap-as-emulated-private-field-AND-brand-check directly (game-state object whose internal fields are private via WeakMap with brand-check for "only-our-emulated-states-pass-this-check"); §Ponyfill+Shim-pattern borrowable for any §new-method-on-existing-prototype where callers might prefer either shape; §Purposeful-Violation-section borrowable as a README shape for §named-deliberate-deviations from fidelity discoverable by future maintainers; §concordance-sniff-defense borrowable wherever §a-diagnostic-library-uses-pattern-matching that the emulation needs to defeat; §capture-before-scuttled borrowable for any §pre-lockdown-utility that needs §prototype-tamper-resistance; ### From endojs/endo packages/hex/{src/encode.js, src/decode.js, index.js, README.md} (Cycle 215 chat-lane 2026-06-07; 172 source lines + ~80 README; @endo/hex is a §ponyfill for the TC39 `Uint8Array.prototype.toHex` / `Uint8Array.fromHex` intrinsics (proposal-arraybuffer-base64, Stage 4); on engines that ship the native intrinsics, the package dispatches to them at module load; on older engines and in SES-locked-down compartments that have removed the intrinsics, the package falls through to a portable pure-JS implementation; **single most structurally interesting move**: §native-error-rerun-polyfill-for-better-diagnostic — on native `Uint8Array.fromHex` throw, re-runs `jsDecodeHex(string, name)` to produce a precise-offset diagnostic with the caller's `name` parameter; falls back to native error if polyfill disagrees; the fast-path-success-path stays cheap (one native call); the error path pays the §quadratic-overhead-but-only-on-failure to get the precise offset and the user-provided `name` in the error message; §the-polyfill-is-the-error-formatter-not-just-the-fallback; §three-named-properties: (1) native-fast-path-stays-fast (no instrumentation overhead); (2) error-path-gets-precise-offset-diagnostic from the polyfill that knows ASCII offsets; (3) if-polyfill-disagrees-with-native (the polyfill would accept what native rejected), fall-back-to-the-native-error (`throw err`); §implementation-defined-native-error-messages-do-not-report-the-failing-offset, so this is not a redundant courtesy — it's the only way to give the user "invalid hex character at offset N of string `<name>`" diagnostics under a native-dispatched binding; §two-different-shapes-for-dispatching-to-native: unconditional for encode (cannot fail on valid input) + dispatch-with-on-failure-polyfill-rerun for decode (can fail on invalid input); §the-asymmetry-is-meaningful: §encode-cannot-fail-on-valid-input but §decode-can-fail-on-invalid-input; §the-exported-binding-is-set-once at module evaluation; no per-call branching, no post-load reconfiguration; §the-public-API-is-just-encodeHex / `decodeHex`; the pure-JS fallbacks `jsEncodeHex` / `jsDecodeHex` are §also-exported-for-benchmarking-and-for-environments-without-the-native-intrinsic; §capture-pre-lockdown-then-rely-on-immutability is the same shape `@endo/env-options` (cycle 207) uses for primordials capture, and the same shape the SES error-handling cluster uses; eleventh §SES-defense-family member in the library: §race-against-lockdown-to-snapshot-intrinsics + §post-lockdown-freezing-makes-the-snapshot-load-bearing; §capture-Reflect.apply-once-at-module-load — the fourth canonical uncurry shape; adds a fourth concrete instance to the §three-canonical-uncurry-shapes-in-endo lineage (cycle 199 trampoline-memoize-nat trio `bind.bind(bind.call)` + cycle 207 env-options `Reflect.apply` + cycle 211 @endo/common `Function.prototype.call.bind` + cycle 215 @endo/hex `Reflect.apply` revisit); §the-comment-is-explicit-about-why: *we prefer it to `Function.prototype.call` even where `.call` is assumed to be primordial, so a tampered `Function.prototype.call` cannot redirect the dispatched native intrinsic invocation*; §Reflect.apply-as-the-defensive-uncurry-against-Function.prototype.call-tampering; §pure-JS-fallback design choices: `jsEncodeHex` (60 lines) — §pre-allocate-the-output-array (`new Array(bytes.length * 2)`) §to-avoid-quadratic-time-string-concatenation; §index-into-a-16-character-alphabet-string for nibble→char mapping; final `chars.join('')` keeps a single string allocation; §lowercase-only with §caller-uppercases-if-needed as the explicit API contract; `jsDecodeHex` (112 lines) — §direct-nibble-computation-from-charcodes (no lookup table); §benchmark-result-noted-in-comment with §benchmark-file-named (`test/decode.bench.js` for the variants): *Computes nibble values directly from character codes rather than indexing a lookup table. On V8 (Node 22), this is roughly 2.5 to 3 times faster than the table-based decoder for ~1 MiB inputs and avoids any module-scope mutable data*; §XS-different-tradeoff-noted: *On XS the polyfill is unavoidably slow regardless of approach; see `test/decode.bench.js` for variants and the relative trade-offs. XS consumers should always reach the native `Uint8Array.fromHex` intrinsic dispatched below as soon as Moddable ships it*; §document-where-the-polyfill-is-known-to-be-slow + §point-at-the-native-intrinsic-as-the-eventual-answer; §`c | 0x20`-fold-uppercase-onto-lowercase trick with §range-check-still-rejects-bit-folded-non-letters — *For ASCII codes: '0' to '9' (48 to 57) -> c - 48; 'a' to 'f' / 'A' to 'F' (97/65 ..) -> (c | 0x20) - 87; `c | 0x20` folds upper- onto lowercase; non-letters with that bit set still fail the (97..102) range check below*; §the-bitwise-OR-doesn't-open-the-door-to-false-positives because §the-range-check-after-the-fold-is-restrictive; §name-for-error-diagnostics parameter — §optional-name-defaults-to-'<unknown>'; the name appears in error messages (`Hex string must have an even length, got ${string.length} in string ${name}` and `Invalid hex character at offset ${i * 2} of string ${name}`); §harden-every-export — `harden(jsEncodeHex);` `harden(jsDecodeHex);` `harden(encodeHex);` `harden(decodeHex);`; §every-exported-function-is-hardened (the polyfills, the dispatched defaults, all four);
